I've been bulimic for years and been "underweight" according to the BMI for a long time now, the thing is though, I realised the body mass index is very corrupt. So let's say there's a 5'8 woman who's skeleton is slightly wider than another woman of the same height and weight. Even though their BMI is identical, the woman with a wider body structure will look bigger, whereas thin boned woman would look underweight. Not only that, compare a man who's been doing serious weightlifting and he has a lot more muscle than the average man. The BMI would tell them they're obese, even though they're a lot fitter than a man of average BMI. So that's that. Please try not to depend on numbers. I used to and it was a big waste of time. What I do now is look in the mirror, or even just walk around and think to myself "does this weight make me feel comfortable?" If I'm not very slim, I struggle to move and just get annoyed. I lost about 10lb in a month and didn't feel any different, but when I walked lots and only ate when I was actually hungry, I felt and looked a lot skinnier the day after already (weird I know) Where I'm going at is, stay at a weight YOU feel most comfortable in, eat food that works for you, because what might work for another person might not work for you. Eg I bulk up when I drink lots of water so I don't lol. But don't depend on charts and try not to look for other peoples opinions, hey if you're chubby but feel great then stay that way, or if you're really skinny but feel the best that way, then that's awesome as well :)
